Operator: Good day, and welcome to the TeleMedia Corp Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a telephone, or click the Q&A icon in the webcast platform if joining online. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to TeleMedia Corp's Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Thornton, Chief Network Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Commercial Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Jordan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We're very pleased with our performance in the second quarter, driven by strong execution and a favorable market environment. We are focused on delivering long-term sustainable growth.

Our achievements include substantial progress in our fiber buildout, where we've constructed over 4,200 route miles this quarter, up 28% year-over-year, bringing our footprint to 12.8 million homes and businesses passed, with 3.9 million fiber subscribers and a take rate of 30.5%. We are also seeing substantial growth from service revenues across wireless up 6.2%, broadband up 3.8%, and enterprise up 2.1% year-over-year. Further, we are concentrating on optimizing our revenue mix, with wireless at 42%, wireline broadband at 28%, media and entertainment at 18%, and enterprise at 12%. Additionally, churn rates have improved to a blended 1.12%, with postpaid wireless at 0.92%. We are also improving our subscriber acquisition costs, trending down 12% year-over-year to $428 per new subscriber. We are strategically investing in operating expense management initiatives that delivered meaningful savings while protecting key investments. Finally, our EBITDA margin expanded to 38.2%, up 320 basis points year-over-year, reflecting strong revenue mix shifts and cost efficiencies.

Sarah Chen: Thank you, Jordan. Moving to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $14.2 billion, representing a 4.5% year-over-year increase. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.42 billion, resulting in a margin of 38.2%. We continue to manage our expenses prudently and are optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures were $2.8 billion year-to-date, primarily focused on expanding our 5G network and fiber infrastructure.

Let me dive deeper into our operating expense management initiatives and their direct impact on profitability. We've made substantial progress, delivering significant net OpEx savings for the year to date while protecting our strategic investments in 5G Standalone core networks, next-gen fiber-to-the-x deployments, and our streaming platform, StreamHub. These efforts have driven our adjusted EBITDA higher, with margins expanding meaningfully. We've focused on headcount and organizational efficiencies, completing a global workforce optimization that reduced non-frontline headcount through attrition, voluntary severance, and targeted restructuring, generating hundreds of millions in annualized savings in SG&A and network operations, all while preserving field technician and customer-facing teams to maintain our strong Net Promoter Score. In our Media segment, AI-driven automation for content curation and ad operations has cut editorial and production overhead substantially.

On vendor and procurement rationalization, we've renegotiated a large portion of our top vendor contracts, achieving double-digit cost reductions, with key wins in spectrum leasing tied to performance-based pricing with tower companies, and optimized content licensing deals at lower rates per subscriber while accelerating zero-rated FAST channels on StreamHub. We've dual-sourced critical customer premises equipment from diverse vendors to mitigate inflation.

Technology-led cost transformation has been a differentiator in our Telecom/Media convergence, with software-defined networking and network function virtualization rollout reducing legacy maintenance costs significantly, funding Open RAN pilots. In Media, machine learning for personalized recommendations has lowered customer acquisition costs, and predictive analytics cut content delivery network fees through edge caching partnerships. We've also migrated legacy mainframes to cloud providers, slashing data center power and cooling expenses amid rising energy costs.

Regionally, North America has delivered the bulk of savings with OpEx down year-over-year, driven by fiber efficiencies and ARPU growth from 5G upgrades. Europe benefited from regulatory tailwinds trimming roaming costs, and Asia-Pacific saw margin expansion through shared infrastructure models. Overall, OpEx as a percentage of revenue has declined steeply, with quarterly reductions supporting free cash flow growth and shareholder returns like dividend increases and buybacks. These savings fuel profitable growth, insulating us from macro headwinds, and we'll sustain run-rate savings into next year via AI operations centers and further optimizations.

Turning to our EBITDA margin performance at 38.2% for the quarter, up 320 basis points year-over-year from 35.0% and 110 basis points sequentially. This marks our strongest quarterly margin in years, on track for full-year guidance. Adjusted EBITDA excludes non-recurring items like spectrum impairments. Margin expansion comes from revenue growth, cost discipline, and our Efficiency First initiative.

Revenue mix shift toward high-margin services drove much of this, with wireless at 52% of revenue delivering 45.6% segment margins on 5G adoption and postpaid ARPU growth from premium plans bundled with streaming. Fiber broadband generated strong margins on revenue growth with low churn. Media contributed via synergies despite some compression. This mix added meaningful basis points as high-margin areas outpaced legacy.

Opex discipline realized sequential savings from AI-powered network operations center automation reducing maintenance costs, bad debt declines from better credit scoring, marketing efficiencies with addressable TV, and vendor optimizations like tower leases and content deals. Capex intensity focused on high-ROI 5G and fiber, with asset divestitures reducing depreciation.

Geographically, North America drove most expansion with strong wireless margins from spectrum utilization and enterprise adjacencies. Europe faced regulatory pressures but improved on FTTH traction, and Asia-Pacific held steady. Trends show accelerating sequential gains, outpacing peers, with leading indicators like 5G traffic and fiber take rates pointing to continued leverage.

Strategically, we're investing in converged 5G-fiber ecosystems, content-tech convergence, and AI/sustainability for green networks, targeting further margin expansion. Risks include spectrum costs and regulatory scrutiny, but our cash flow provides flexibility.

On service revenue growth, total service revenues hit $14.2 billion, up 4.5% adjusted year-over-year, with wireless at +6.2% to $8.9 billion on postpaid adds and ARPU from 5G plans and nationwide SA core deployment. Broadband up 3.8% to $3.4 billion, led by fiber growth and multi-gig speeds. Enterprise up 2.1% to $1.9 billion on private 5G and edge services. This underscores our Fiber First, 5G Everywhere strategy, with full-year growth outlook of 4-5%.

For revenue mix, wireless services contributed 42% at $12.1 billion full-year equivalent pace, up 12% on 5G and bundling. Wireline broadband 28% up 6% on FTTH adds. Media and entertainment 18% up 14% on streaming subs and FAST. Enterprise and wholesale 12% up 9% on private networks. This diversification lifts ARPU and revenue quality, with digital/recurring at 82%, guiding 9-11% growth next year.

Blended SAC trended to $428 per new subscriber, down 12% year-over-year, with postpaid wireless at $412, broadband at $520, and streaming lower. Marketing efficiencies from AI targeting, optimized channel mix, and device subsidies normalization drove this. Regionally, North America led declines, APAC strongest. LTV remains well above SAC multiples, guiding lower into 2025.

Mike Thornton: Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our network performance. We've made significant strides in expanding our 5G coverage and increasing network capacity. We're also investing in advanced technologies like network slicing and edge computing to support new applications and services. Our network uptime and reliability remain high. We are also improving fiber buildout progress, with 12.8 million homes and businesses now passed after adding 2.1 million this quarter through density-focused deployments in Sunbelt, Texas, Midwest, and Northeast regions, leveraging grants and partnerships. Subscriber adoption hit 3.9 million, up 420,000, with 30.5% take rate, residential ARPU at $112, business growth, and low 0.9% monthly churn. This validates our fiber-plus-hybrid approach, on track for more passings and adds ahead.

Lisa Patel: Thank you. We've seen strong customer growth and improved customer satisfaction scores this quarter. Our bundled service offerings are resonating well with customers, and we're focused on providing a seamless and personalized customer experience. We are also focused on increasing churn rate improvements, with blended at 1.12% down 12 basis points year-over-year, postpaid wireless at 0.92%, broadband 1.08%, driven by network leadership, OneBill bundles, and AI retention models intervening with at-risk customers. Video saw some pressure from cord-cutting, but regions like North America excel. We're advancing technical initiatives like Open RAN and Customer 360 for sub-1% goals.

Raj Singh: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to enhance our network and services. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations and improve efficiency. We are also working on developing new products and services that leverage 5G and edge computing. Our R&D efforts are concentrated on advancing SDN, NFV, Open RAN pilots, cloud migrations, and AI for media personalization and predictive maintenance.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your plans for expanding your presence in the enterprise market and how you plan to compete with existing players, specifically regarding service revenue growth in enterprise?

Lisa Patel: Thanks for the question, John. In enterprise, we're growing service revenues 2.1% year-over-year to $1.9 billion, resilient amid IT spend caution. Wireless enterprise up 5.4% on 112,000 net adds via 5G private networks and Managed Connectivity as a Service, serving 40% of Fortune 1000. Key wins like multi-year deals for CBRS private 5G enable AR and IoT. Wired flat but cloud interconnects up 11%, offset by legacy declines. Edge Computing alliances position us for the $15 billion opportunity, with Q2 services up 18%. North America drives 80%, EMEA softer, but EBITDA margin at 52% from Open RAN efficiencies. Our Fiber First and 5G strategy expands dedicated fiber and low-latency services, competing via integrated bundles outpacing pure-play rivals.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for the impact of inflation and rising interest rates on your business, and how do you plan to mitigate those risks, especially regarding operating expense management initiatives?

Sarah Chen: Great question, Emily. Inflation and rates pressure costs, but our OpEx initiatives delivered $450 million sequential savings, exceeding guidance, flowing to EBITDA. Headcount optimization saved $450 million annualized, vendor renegotiations $350 million with 11% blended cuts, tech transformation $280 million from SDN/NFV and cloud migrations cutting power OpEx. Dual-sourcing CPE mitigated 7-9% inflation. OpEx/revenue fell to 61.5%, Q4 down 5%. Regionally, North America OpEx down 7.2%, Europe roaming cuts 14%, APAC flat but margins up. This insulates profitability, boosting FCF 15%, funding dividends and buybacks. Phase 2 AI ops and arbitrage sustain $800 million run-rate into '24, offsetting macro via hybrid economics lifting retention and ARPU.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee: Can you discuss your sustainability initiatives and your plans for reducing your carbon footprint, and how will you measure your success, specifically addressing EBITDA margin trends?

Jordan Hale: Thanks, David. Sustainability is core, tying to green networks with 30% lower power via liquid cooling for EU ETS credits and 5-7% opex cuts, enhancing margins. Our 38.2% EBITDA margin up 320 bps YoY from mix to high-margin wireless 45.6% and fiber 42%, opex savings 40% of expansion via AI NOC and vendor optimizations. North America drove 70%, outpacing peers. Trends accelerating with third straight 100+ bps sequential gains, churn low, traffic up 40%. Pillars like converged ecosystems, content convergence, AI/sustainability target 40%+ by 2025, measured by EBITDAaL 41%, fiber take rates 55%, and annual 200+ bps expansion, with ROI-positive capex.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Jordan, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Jordan Hale: Thank you. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainable growth. Thank you for your time and interest in TeleMedia Corp.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

aspect_summary.Fiber buildout: progress, coverage expan: 12.8M homes/businesses passed (added 2.1M this quarter, 4,200+ route miles up 28% YoY); 3.9M subscribers (up 420k), 30.5% take rate.

aspect_summary.Churn rate analysis: trends and drivers: Blended 1.12% (down 12 bps YoY); postpaid wireless 0.92%, broadband 1.08%; driven by network leadership, OneBill bundles, AI retention models.
